facts.F1: ADO Story 6504: Choose whether a Feature without children gets an inferred size. Today a Feature with no child Work Items is sized by the Portfolio's Default Feature Size and that count is spread across the teams (e.g. '0 of 4'); some users read it as data from the tracker. Want a setting: Infer (today's behaviour, clearly labelled as an assumption wherever the count shows) or Disable (no inferred count; the Feature shows no remaining work and says it has no child Work Items yet). Open: what a forecast does for such a Feature when inference is off. Source: customer feedback 2026-11-02 ('No guessing when an item has no children ... I'd rather see nothing, or a clear label saying it's an assumption'). Maintainer skipped DISCOVER and DIVERGE explicitly on 2026-11-25; stand-alone Story, no parent Epic.

facts.F3: A Portfolio owner can switch default (inferred) Feature sizing off. When it is off, a Feature with no child Work Items gets size 0: Lighthouse invents no count for it and assigns nothing to any Team, and forecasts take that 0 as it comes. When it is on, Lighthouse behaves as today.
facts.F30: With the switch off, a not-Done Feature with no child Work Items gets size 0: no inferred count, no remaining work assigned to any Team, and forecasts take the 0 as it comes.
facts.F31: A per-Portfolio on/off switch for default Feature sizing in the advanced settings next to Default Feature Size, on for existing and new Portfolios.
facts.F32: With the switch off, the Feature shows the note 'No child Work Items yet' in today's warning-icon place in the Feature lists on the Portfolio and Team pages and on the Delivery timeline.
facts.F33: With the switch off, the override real child count states rule and a mapped size-estimate field have no effect: a Feature's size is its real child count, or 0.
facts.F34: With the switch off, Default Feature Size, the percentile option, the size-estimate field mapping and the override-states selection are greyed out; their stored values are kept and come back when the switch is on again.
facts.F35: Special forecast handling for a Feature sized 0 (skipping it, showing no date, warnings on the forecast): excluded because the maintainer decided the forecast takes the 0 as it comes.
facts.F36: A new or stronger 'assumed' label on inferred counts when the switch is on: excluded because the maintainer did not ask for it; today's warning stays.
facts.F37: Changing how Default Feature Size or its percentile is computed, and rewriting Delivery metrics history or archived Deliveries.
facts.F38: No Epic, because 6504 is a single stand-alone Story (maintainer, 2026-11-25). DISCOVER and DIVERGE were skipped explicitly by the maintainer on 2026-11-25.
facts.F39: One general on/off switch for default (inferred) Feature sizing. On: today's behaviour, unchanged. Off: a Feature with no child Work Items gets size 0, so there is no inferred count and nothing is assigned to any Team (maintainer, 2026-11-25: 'a general switch to turn default size off, then we simply take 0 and live with the consequences').
facts.F4: Default sizing on: a Feature without child Work Items is sized as today
facts.F40: The Story's open forecast question is answered: no special forecast handling. When the switch is off, When / How Many forecasts, Delivery likelihood and the Delivery timeline take the 0 as it comes, whatever that means for dates and likelihood (maintainer, 2026-11-25).
facts.F41: Old records stay as recorded: Delivery metrics history and archived Deliveries keep the 'using default size' flag they were captured with; switching off changes only what is computed from then on.
facts.F42: Done Features, Features that have child Work Items, and the percentile calculation of Default Feature Size are unaffected by the switch.
facts.F43: Every changed view that shows data (Feature lists on Portfolio and Team pages, Delivery timeline, Delivery Feature-size chart, Portfolio advanced settings): what it shows while loading and when loading fails.
facts.F44: Context map placement after ADR-270/ADR-271: which bounded contexts the switch touches (Portfolio configuration, Feature sizing, Forecasting), the glossary term for the switch (proposed 'default Feature sizing'), whether turning it off publishes or reacts to a domain event (proposed: a Portfolio settings-changed event triggers the existing Feature recalculation), and the UI surface (proposed: the Portfolio's settings tab).
facts.F45: End-of-DISCUSS checklist view: RBAC unchanged, the switch is a Portfolio setting edited by whoever edits Portfolio settings today (Portfolio admins). Lighthouse-Clients CLI/MCP: the Portfolio settings payload gains the switch and clients that read or write Portfolio settings must carry it; the Feature payload gains nothing new. Website: one line, e.g. 'Turn off default Feature sizing: a Feature without child Work Items counts as 0, never a guess'. Context map: see the Design open decision.
facts.F46: No labelling change when the switch is on: the existing warning icon and sentence stay; no stronger 'assumed' mark (maintainer, 2026-11-25).
facts.F47: Switching default sizing off also turns off the 'override real child count states' rule. Off means Lighthouse never puts a default size in place of real children: a Feature's size is its real child count, or 0 if it has none (maintainer, 2026-11-25).
facts.F48: The switch lives per Portfolio in its advanced settings next to Default Feature Size. It is on for existing and new Portfolios, so nothing changes on upgrade (maintainer, 2026-11-25).
facts.F49: With the switch off, a Feature with no child Work Items shows 0 remaining Work Items plus the note 'No child Work Items yet' in today's warning-icon place: the Feature lists on the Portfolio and Team pages and the Delivery timeline (maintainer, 2026-11-25).

facts.F50: With the switch off, a mapped size-estimate field does not size a Feature: always 0 without children. And we shouldn't even be able to set any other value/option in the default feature size').
